QF.id: XXVA Regulatory Compliance for Non-Core Research Personnel_18

question.text: A part-time research analyst under SEBI RA Regulations is:

answer.text: Any analyst who works fewer than 8 hours a day
A person who provides research services on a part-time basis and is also engaged in other permitted business activities
An analyst who only covers small-cap stocks
Any analyst who has been in the profession for less than 2 years

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI's research-analyst framework, a part-time research analyst is conceptually a person who provides research services on a part-time basis while simultaneously being engaged in other permitted business or professional activities. The category exists to accommodate professionals whose research work is one of several streams of activity rather than their sole full-time pursuit. The Trap: Part-time status does not turn on a numerical hours-per-day threshold, on whether the analyst covers only small-cap stocks, or on years of experience — it turns on the nature of the analyst's overall engagement. Note: The Series XV Research Analyst workbook pages reviewed mention that the RA definition includes a part-time research analyst and reference Form C/limitations for part-time RAs, but do not state the specific "research on a part-time basis while also engaged in other permitted business activities" definition. The framing above reflects general regulatory practice rather than a workbook citation.
